close_reason: Fixed. Replaced manual match-on-Value with serde_json::from_value::<Option<T>>() per filter arg, propagating shape errors as JmapError::invalid_arguments. Also lifted the args.as_object_mut() borrow into a single block-scope binding instead of re-acquiring it twice. Added 3 regression tests covering non-string filterRelatedType, non-array filterMetadataType, and non-string element inside filterMetadataType. Existing valid-filter and Null-filter tests still pass. All 39 tests pass; clippy clean.
description:
metadata.rs:79-102 — parses filterRelatedType and filterMetadataType. Two issues:

1. Type-coercion permissiveness on wrong shapes:

    filter_related_type: Option<String> = ...
        .and_then(|v| match v {
            Value::String(s) => Some(s),
            Value::Null => None,
            _ => None,    // <-- silently drops e.g. an integer or array
        });

A client sending {"filterRelatedType": 42} or {"filterRelatedType": ["Email"]} gets no error — the field is silently treated as null and all related-types are returned. Same for filterMetadataType — non-array values silently become null, and within an array, non-string elements are silently dropped via filter_map.

Per RFC 8620 §1.6 the server ignores unknown fields, but the spec does NOT permit silent type coercion of recognized fields. A client sending the wrong shape for a recognized field should get invalidArguments.

2. Subtle: args.as_object_mut().and_then(|m| m.remove("filterRelatedType")) is called twice (once for each filter arg). On the second call, the first filter has already been removed. Order-dependent but each remove only fires once, so it works — but the read pattern is fragile and a future contributor adding a third filter will reach for the same pattern, which gets quadratic-shaped quickly.

Compare canonical: jmap_server::handlers::handle_changes (the delegated path other extensions use) does NOT do filter-arg parsing in the shim — it parses since_state and max_changes only, with explicit invalidArguments on wrong shape. The metadata shim diverges to handle the spec's Metadata-specific filter args, but the divergence loses the strictness.

Fix: 
- Use serde_json::from_value::<Option<String>>(v) and from_value::<Option<Vec<String>>>(v) to parse the filter args, propagating serde errors as JmapError::invalid_arguments. Drop the manual match-on-Value pattern.
- Or, define a small typed args struct deserialized once at the top of the handler.

Minor: even after the typed parse, the unknown-fields-on-args question (per §1.6) is fine to leave permissive. The hard requirement is that recognized fields with wrong shape produce invalidArguments.

Severity: P2 because the wrong behavior is silent-success-with-wrong-answer, not data corruption. Users who hit this will receive results that don't match their filter and likely won't notice until they're filing bugs against the wrong layer.
title: Unknown args in Metadata/changes silently accepted; filter parsing is permissive on wrong shapes
